title: PTWC tsunami threat categories (2014-2026) were reached at tide gauges in 29% of threat regions, but in 75% of regions with 11 or more gauges, so sparse gauges explain most of the gap
abstract: The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center (PTWC) gives each threatened country or territory one of four amplitude categories (less than 0.3 m, 0.3-1 m, 1-3 m, more than 3 m) that are possible along some coasts. We parsed all 428 non-test PTWC Pacific and Caribbean threat messages from October 2014 to October 2026 (71 earthquakes, 1,121 event-region pairs). We compared the first- and last-stated category with the maximum NCEI tide-gauge amplitude in the region. The analysis plan was committed before the comparison. 208 pairs in 55 events had gauge records. For 139 threat pairs, the gauge maximum was below the stated category in 69% (event bootstrap 95% interval 60-83%), in it in 29% and above it in 2%. 'Less than 0.3 m' was exceeded in 10% (3-19%). Updates changed only 19 of 208 categories and gave no gain. The shortfall depended strongly on gauge count: 92% below with one gauge, 15% (0-41%) below and 75% exact with 11 or more gauges. In an exploratory check, reading one random gauge in regions with 6 or more gauges raised the below fraction from 27% to 83%. Only 16% of 846 individual gauge records reached the stated category. Thus the categories behave as statements about the regional coastal maximum. They were near calibrated and seldom too low where many gauges existed, but they are upper bounds for a single harbour. The main limitation is that gauges sample the coast sparsely, so the true coastal maximum is unknown in most regions. Also, only 30 pairs had categories of 1 m or more.

display.caption: First-stated PTWC category against the observed category for 208 event-region pairs. Left: NCEI tide-gauge maximum. Right: maximum of tide-gauge, survey and eyewitness values. Numbers are counts and row percentages; orange squares mark agreement.

Fraction of first-stated threat pairs whose gauge maximum was below the stated category, by number of NCEI tide-gauge records in the region (bars, event-bootstrap 95% intervals). Orange: expected fraction when only k random gauges of the 33 pairs with 6 or more gauges are read (exploratory). Green line: the same 33 pairs with all gauges.
Individual tide-gauge maxima (grey) and regional maxima (blue) by first-stated category, log scale; shaded bands are the stated ranges. Values below 0.01 m are drawn at 0.01 m.
